Allergies:
Penicillins

Chief Complaint:
abdominal pain, diarrhea, SOB

History of Present Illness:
Ms. ___ is a ___ female with a history of AF on
eliquis s/p 2 prior ___, h/o DVT/embolus, T2DM, hypothyroidism
and chronic anemia with prior subclinical GI bleed who presents
with 1 week of generalized abdominal pain and diarrhea. 

She was in her usual state of health until about 2 weeks ago 
when
she started not feeling well. She describes general malaise and
loss of appetite 2 weeks ago. She was having a hard time getting
out of bed. She was eating much less, and does feel she has lost
___ lbs since this started. When she did eat, she says food
tasted "bitter" and she feels that her saliva is thick. She
denies fever/chills, urinary sx or n/v at this time. She does 
say
that she began eating out more this past week (which she 
normally
does not do, normally cooks at home) in an attempt to overcome
her loss of appetite. 

One week ago, she developed watery diarrhea that occurred
___. She is also having diarrhea overnight, about 4x/night.
She says the diarrhea was watery, loose, and dark-colored (which
is her baseline from taking iron supplements). She denies red
blood in the stool. She does endorse some incontinence with her
stools, including incontinence at night and going in the bed. 
She
also endorses diffuse abdominal pain at this time that would
precede an episode of diarrhea, and subsequently improvement. 
She
describes abdominal pain as a general ache all over her belly,
with no radiation. She did not take anything for the abd pain or
diarrhea. She denies fever/chills, dizziness/syncope,
headaches/vision changes, or urinary sx. No vomiting, although
she says she had some nausea this morning only which was
self-limiting. She denies any recent sick contacts or travel. 
She
has never had c diff before. A few weeks ago, she was started on
minocycline for acne outbreaks on her face and chest. She also
has itching, for which she uses cream. 

She also describes shortness of breath, which has been going on
since her admission in ___, per below. At this time, she was
started on Furosemide 20mg daily. She becomes SOB within 
exertion
only, occurs with taking a few steps. She does have a history of
HFpEF, and 2 weeks ago noted that her PCP doubled her ___
to 20mg BID. She says that her SOB has improved just slightly
since then. She has not been on Furosemide prior to ___. She
says her PCP did make ___ note to her about her kidney function,
and said she would need to follow up. 

Of note, she was admitted in ___ for evaluation of SOB, fatigue
and chest discomfort. She was treated for CHF exacerbation, AF
with RVR and CAP. TTE revealed preserved EF. She had undergone
successful DCCV in ___ but was noted to be back in AF on her
previous admission. She was referred for repeat DCCV procedure
upon discharge which was done ___ . Amiodarone was initiated
at this time of most recent cardioversion. She says she cannot
tell when she is in AF. 

She endorses a dry mouth for a few weeks, for which she has been
taking Biotene and has noted improvement with this.  She denies
skin/hair/nail changes. Denies CP. She previously had ___ edema
prior, improved recently with increase in Furosemide dose.

In the ED:

- Initial vital signs were notable for:
T 97.8 F, HR 50, BP 136/57, RR 18, O2 98% RA

- Exam notable for:
Abdominal/GI: Mild diffuse abdominal tenderness to palpation 
Renal: No CVA tenderness
MSK: Right arm deformity since birth, otherwise no signs of
trauma, no focal deficits noted
Neuro: Sensation intact upper and lower extremities, strength 
___
upper and lower, CN II-XII intact, moving all extremities

- Labs were notable for:
BUN 65, Creatinine 2.4, Anion gap 18, ALT 46, AST 60, Lactate 
2.2

WBCs 8, Hb 13.4, Hct 40.5, BNP 363 
Troponin <0.01 

Blood culture pending 

- Studies performed include:
CXR  - IMPRESSION: Suspected right lower lobar atelectasis,
similar to prior. No acute intrathoracic abnormality.

ECG: Sinus bradycardia, T wave inversions in V2 to V6

- Patient was given:
750mL IVF

Vitals on transfer: 
HR 46, BP 103/76, RR 17, O2 100% RA

Upon arrival to the floor, she says she does not currently have
abdominal pain and is not currently feeling the need to have a
BM. ROS negative per above. Denies n/v, fever/chills or
lightheadedness. 

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Other ROS obtained and is otherwise negative.

Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY STATEMENT:
====================
The patient is a ___ female with a history of atrial 
fibrillation on Eliquis, non-insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes, 
hypothyroidism, chronic anemia who came in with 1 week of 
generalized abdominal pain and diarrhea, found to have an AK I. 
On admission she was given IV fluids, with subsequent resolution 
of her ___. Her diarrhea resolved without intervention. A C. 
difficile two-step stool test was negative. She also had dyspnea 
on exertion, pharmacologic nuclear cardiac stress test was 
negative for reversible ischemia and showed only septal 
hypokinesis. She was initially bradycardic, but upon flipping 
into atrial fibrillation bordered on the edge of tachycardia. 
She was maintained on her home metoprolol rate control, 
amiodarone, and apixaban. She was discharged home following 
resolution of her diarrhea and ___.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
==============
#Diarrhea
#Hypovolemia
Patient noted over a week of diarrhea on admission. However, 
this self resolved during her admission. She was given IV 
fluids. Her stool was negative for C. difficile. Stool cultures 
were not sent.

#Prerenal acute kidney injury
Patient noted to have a significantly elevated creatinine on 
admission. It was determined likely secondary to prerenal ___ in 
the setting of significant fluid losses given significant 
improvement with rehydration. On discharge her creatinine was 
1.0.

#Dyspnea on exertion
Patient complained of dyspnea on exertion when she was admitted. 
Given concern for flow-limiting coronary artery disease, patient 
had a nuclear pharmacologic cardiac stress test on ___, 
which showed septal hypokinesis but no reversible myocardial 
perfusion defects. To follow-up the study, she had a TTE on 
___ which showed mild symmetric left ventricular 
hypertrophy with normal size and regional/global biventricular 
systolic function. Abnormal septal motion was noted on TTE. She 
also had mild to moderate tricuspid regurgitation and mild 
pulmonary artery systolic hypertension.

#Bradycardia
#Atrial fibrillation/flutter with RVR
Patient was noted to be in sinus bradycardia on admission. Rates 
were as low as 43. Her home metoprolol was held briefly. However 
later in the admission, she was noted to be in atrial 
fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and a mean 
ventricular rate in the low 100s. She has also experienced 
atrial flutter with ___ block. Thus metoprolol was restarted, at 
a lower dose. Given her heart rate below 60 on discharge, she 
was maintained on this dose (metoprolol tartrate 50 mg twice 
daily).

CHRONIC ISSUES:
===============
#HFpEF
As noted above, home Lasix was held in the setting of prerenal 
___ and significant fluid losses through diarrhea. On discharge 
Lasix continue to be held. Defer to PCP/cardiology for 
management of diuretic.

#Hypothyroidism
-Continued home levothyroxine 

#ASCVD Risk
#Non-insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Metformin was held and patient was placed on insulin sliding 
scale while inpatient. Metformin restarted on discharge. Started 
rosuvastatin this admission.

#GERD
-Continued home omeprazole.

#Acne
-Held home minocycline, and on discharge.

#Insomnia
-Continued home lorazepam qhs.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
====================
[ ] Patient was noted to be bradycardic while in sinus rhythm on 
admission, likely secondary to dose of beta-blocker, but 
tachycardic while in atrial fibrillation/flutter. Defer to 
primary cardiologist for workup of possible tachy-brady syndrome 
and further management of rate/rhythm control.

[ ] Home Lasix was held following this admission, as patient was 
significantly dehydrated with prerenal ___ due to diarrhea. 
Given that she had shortness of breath on 20 mg Lasix daily in 
the past, she will likely need to restart her diuretic at the 
higher dose on follow-up. Defer to Dr. ___ for management.

[ ] Given patient's ASCVD risk, she was started on rosuvastatin 
20 mg daily.

CONTACT:
Name of health care proxy: ___ 
Relationship: daughter 
Cell phone: ___ 
CODE STATUS: full

Discharge Diagnosis:
PRIMARY DIAGNOSES:
Diarrhea
Acute kidney injury secondary to dehydration
Atrial fibrillation
Bradycardia

SECONDARY DIAGNOSES:
Transaminitis
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
Hypothyroidism
GERD
Insomnia
